A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same molecular-synthesis framework despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original analog-generation, molecular-optimization, docking, and ablation results in Tables 1–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds template-extrapolation, sampled-training, and convergence experiments in Appendices B and F.

M1.justification: v2 adds an optional training procedure that samples C masks per program each epoch instead of enumerating all masks. The stated GA selection rule also changes from early diversity-based and later GP-based selection to GP expected-improvement selection between siblings. The core bilevel framework, networks, losses, and auxiliary prediction task remain.

E1.justification: The synthetic-tree and ChEMBL datasets, 13 main property objectives, and two docking targets remain. The standalone QED optimization comparison in v1 Table 4 disappears, although QED remains a data filter. The new appendix experiments otherwise reuse existing datasets and objectives.

E2.justification: The 25-method external benchmark suite and existing SynNet comparisons remain; shortening Table 2 does not remove those methods from the full results. New ablation comparisons introduce the reduced-template EP and sampled-training MC1/MC10 variants against the standard model.

E3.justification: v2 adds a frequency-stratified template holdout, retraining policies while retaining the original recognizer, plus k=4 controls and C=1/10 mask-sampling experiments. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Table 2 also changes its stated budget from 10,000 to 1,000 oracle calls, contradicting v2 Appendix H's retained 10,000-call protocol; this does not establish that the benchmark was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds structural-extrapolation and template-set robustness studies. Appendices F.5 and F.7 add sampling sensitivity, downstream performance tradeoffs, and training-convergence analysis. Existing decoding-order, sibling-generation, auxiliary-task, recognition, attention, and docking analyses largely remain.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained Table 4 comparisons preserve their population mean-and-spread summaries. Added mask-count statistics extend existing descriptive reporting rather than introduce a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: The original analog results and full per-oracle numerical tables are retained. New k=4 experiments report recovery rates of 52% versus 56% for EP versus standard training, and 36%/65% versus 56% for MC1/MC10 versus standard training, alongside new optimization and convergence results. QED results and some aggregate and docking metric entries are removed. These additions use new experimental conditions, rather than demonstrate a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Section 4.1.3 and Appendix F.7 add asymptotic reasoning about mask enumeration, precomputation, and sampled-training costs relative to SynNet. The existing grammar, MDP formulation, and loss mathematics are otherwise substantially retained, with revised notation and exposition.

C1.justification: The abstract, consolidated contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a program-synthesis formulation, separation of syntax and semantics, advantages on both molecular tasks, and control over synthesis resources. The additional studies do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of template removal and mask sampling as regularization, discusses stronger degradation on ChEMBL, and explains task-dependent efficiency–performance tradeoffs. Table 11 newly qualifies comparison validity because software versions 1.0.0 and 0.3.6 may produce different Sitagliptin and Zaleplon evaluations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and focused implementation disclosures: the QED > 0.5 filter, batch size 64, NVIDIA RTX A6000 hardware, approximately one/five hours for reaction/building-block network training, GP kernel and fitting details, and evaluation-software versions. Most architecture and GA hyperparameters were already documented.

R1.justification: New Appendix D.3 substantially expands positioning relative to retrosynthesis, self-improving planners, Decision Transformer, and GFlowNets, explaining alternative formulations and possible extensions. It adds relevant citations while the earlier simulated-annealing and particle-swarm connections and several associated references disappear.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, its authorship/header changes, and substantial methodology and ablation passages are rewritten. Notation is simplified, training steps become Algorithm 1, related-work sections are reorganized, the conclusion is shortened, and appendix material is redistributed and expanded.

P2.justification: The main displays are substantially redesigned: Figure 2 becomes side-by-side, Table 1 incorporates the previous decoding ablation, Table 2 becomes a compact category-based summary, and Table 3 merges docking panels. New extrapolation, sampling, mask-count, and convergence displays supplement extensive relocation and reformatting.

improvement.justification: The new robustness and training-efficiency studies address previously untested questions, while clearer presentation, implementation disclosures, and the software-version qualification improve usability and transparency. These gains are limited by new reporting problems: Table 2 contradicts Appendix H on the oracle budget, and Figure 14 has an EP caption for MC results and apparently duplicated values across different objectives. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
